concepts.why: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion along the anterosuperior wall of the urinary bladder, as seen on ultrasound and CT scans, is consistent with a bladder papilloma.
The patient's symptoms of dysuria and hematuria, along with the presence of red and pus cells in the urine, suggest a urinary tract infection.
The patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a cystic area in the left adnexa, as seen on ultrasound, are consistent with endometriosis.
The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation, as seen on CT scan, is consistent with a kidney stone.
The presence of a left hydrosalpinx, as seen on CT scan, is consistent with a diagnosis of hydrosalpinx.
The patient's symptoms of dysuria and the presence of a left hydrosalpinx, as seen on CT scan, suggest a diagnosis of pelvic inflammatory disease.
The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion along the anterosuperior wall of the urinary bladder, as seen on ultrasound and CT scans, could also be consistent with bladder cancer.

The patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a cystic area in the left adnexa, as seen on ultrasound, along with the presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion along the anterosuperior wall of the urinary bladder, could be consistent with an endometriotic cyst of the bladder.

rationales.F01: Right flank pain is a non-specific symptom that can be associated with kidney stones.
rationales.F03: Hematuria is a common symptom of bladder cancer and urinary bladder papilloma.
rationales.F04: Abdominal hysterectomy may be related to endometriosis.
rationales.F06: The focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion is highly suggestive of a bladder tumor.
rationales.F09: The well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks is highly suggestive of a bladder tumor.
rationales.F11: The right calyceal calculus is a strong indicator of a kidney stone.
rationales.F12: The left hydrosalpinx is a strong indicator of a gynecological condition such as endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease.
